title: Phase 7: sprints, planning, burndown and velocity
body:
## What

Sprint planning (FR-5). Projects get sprints you can plan, start and complete. There is a backlog view, a burndown chart for the active sprint, and a velocity chart across completed sprints. Starting or completing a sprint notifies project members through the transactional outbox.

## How

- **API (`apps/api/src/sprints`)**
  - Endpoints to list, get, create, update and delete sprints. Only planned sprints can be deleted.
  - Start and complete a sprint; add issues to a sprint and remove them.
  - `GET …/burndown` and `GET …/velocity`.
- **Integrity**
  - One ACTIVE sprint per project is enforced by a partial unique index. A race on start returns 409 (P2002 is mapped).
  - Sprint rows are locked with `FOR UPDATE` while they change.
  - Each issue move records its outcome in `sprint_issues`: COMPLETED, REMOVED or CARRIED_OVER.
  - Each issue move also writes a `SPRINT_CHANGED` issue event.
- **Completing a sprint** moves open issues to the backlog or to another planned sprint (`moveOpenIssuesTo`).
- **Burndown** is computed from issue history by the pure function `computeBurndown`, which has its own unit tests. Velocity comes from `sprint_issues`.
- **Notifications**
  - `sprint.started` and `sprint.completed` events go through the outbox and fan out to members.
  - The notification payload types are now a discriminated union by type (`describeNotification`, `notificationHref`).
- **Issues**
  - The issue list filter accepts `sprint=<id>|active|none`, and `IssueSummary` includes `sprint`.
  - The board is scoped to the active sprint, with a toggle to show all issues.
- **Web**
  - A new Sprints tab with the active sprint, planned sprints and the backlog, plus create and complete dialogs.
  - Burndown and velocity are hand-rolled SVG charts using validated `--chart-1` and `--chart-2` tokens.
  - Charts have hover and keyboard tooltips, and a data table for each chart.

## Testing

- Full `pnpm check` passes: 18/18 tasks and 469 tests.
  - types: 134
  - API: 76 unit, 13 HTTP, 154 integration (Testcontainers)
  - web: 76
  - AI: 16
- New tests:
  - `burndown.spec.ts` (7 tests)
  - `sprints-api.int-spec.ts` (9 tests: lifecycle, the ACTIVE race, carry-over, RBAC, archived projects)
  - A sprint fan-out test in `notifications.int-spec.ts`
  - Web tests for the charts and dialogs
- Mutation check: I removed the catch for the sprint unique violation and the race test failed. I then restored it.
- I ran a 12-step browser check against a throwaway compose stack:
  - Burndown showed "23 of 31 committed points remaining".
  - Completing PAY Sprint 2 carried 4 issues into Sprint 3.
  - The board showed the 5 sprint cards and 9 cards when set to show all issues.
  - The developer view was read-only.
  - Sprint notifications were delivered.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes (lint, typecheck, tests in every package)
- [x] Docs updated (architecture, API, README) where behaviour changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens or personal data in code, tests or logs

title: Phase 6b: attachments, transactional outbox and notifications
body:
## What

The second half of issue tracking:
- **Attachments (FR-4.6):** files upload straight from the browser to object storage.
- **In-app notifications with assignment email (FR-12):** events are delivered through a transactional outbox, so a change and its notification can never disagree.

## How

**Attachments**
- **Upload flow:**
  1. Request an upload.
  2. The browser `PUT`s the file straight to storage using a pre-signed URL.
  3. Complete the upload.
- Size, type and `Content-Disposition` are part of the URL's signature, so storage rejects any other body with `403`.
- On completion the API checks the size and type of the stored object. If they don't match, it deletes the object and the record.
- **Rules:**
  - A type allow-list: images, PDF, text, CSV, Markdown, JSON, zip and gzip. HTML, SVG, XML and script types are never allowed.
  - At most 10 MB per file and 50 files per issue.
  - File names are sanitised; storage keys are random.
- **Downloads** use pre-signed links valid for 60 seconds and are always served as `attachment`.
- **Delete:** the uploader or a project manager can delete a file; the object is removed from storage first.
- An hourly worker job removes uploads that were never completed.
- **Local storage is SeaweedFS** (in Compose and Testcontainers), because MinIO no longer publishes container images (ADR-0011).
  - The app uses only the S3 API through AWS SDK v3, so AWS S3 works without code changes.
  - In dev, the API creates the bucket and its CORS rule. This setup is non-fatal: a storage outage never stops the API from starting.

**Transactional outbox → notifications (ADR-0006, now built)**
- Issue assignment and new comments write `outbox_events` rows in the same transaction as the change.
- **The worker's relay publishes those rows:**
  - It claims rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so several relays can run safely.
  - It is woken by a `pg_notify` trigger, which fires only on commit, with a 500 ms poll as the fallback.
  - Job IDs are deterministic (`outbox-{id}`).
  - If Redis fails, the transaction rolls back and the rows stay pending.
- **The notification processor:**
  - Reloads the current state and skips stale events, such as reassigned or deleted issues, self-assignment, or people who have left the project.
  - Inserts with a per-recipient `dedupe_key`, so a redelivered event creates nothing.
- **Who is notified:**
  - The assignee, who also gets an email.
  - For comments: the reporter, the assignee and earlier commenters, but never the author.
- Published outbox rows are pruned daily.
- **Endpoints:** list (keyset pagination), unread count, mark read and read-all. You only ever see your own notifications.

**Web**
- An attachments panel with upload progress, download and delete.
- A notification bell with an unread badge that refreshes every 30 seconds.
- A notifications page with "Mark all as read".
- Attachment events appear in the issue history.

## Testing

- A clean run of `pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test build --force` passed all 18 tasks, **432 tests**:
  - Types: 127
  - API: 69 unit, 13 HTTP and 143 integration tests against real Postgres, Redis and SeaweedFS
  - Web: 64
  - AI service: 16
- New integration tests:
  - **Attachments (8):**
    - the full upload/download flow
    - storage rejecting a wrong size or type (`403`)
    - an upload that doesn't match its request being discarded
    - validation and permissions
    - delete removing the object from storage
    - archived projects and deleted issues
    - cleanup of abandoned uploads
  - **Outbox and notifications (10):**
    - the outbox row is written inside the transaction, and none is written for a rejected edit
    - re-publishing collapses into the existing job
    - three relays draining 250 rows never publish one twice
    - the relay loop publishes promptly and shuts down cleanly
    - pruning
    - idempotent fan-out, with the email sent once
    - stale and self-assignment events are skipped
    - comment recipients
    - API pagination, read state and isolation between users
- **Mutation checks** (each was reverted afterwards):
  - Without `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, the concurrent-relay test fails 3/3.
  - Without the dedupe key, the redelivery test fails.
  - Without the stored-object check, the mismatch test fails.
- **Browser run with the real worker, 12 steps, all passing:**
  - upload and download (identical content)
  - an SVG refused before upload
  - history entries
  - Sam's unread badge, then opening the notification to reach the issue
  - the assignment email arriving in Mailpit
  - a comment notifying the reporter
  - "Mark all as read"
  - delete
- The browser run found a real bug: Chrome reports `.log` files as `text/x-log`, which made the client refuse them. It is fixed: the extension is now the fallback, script-capable types are still refused, and there are regression tests.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes (lint, typecheck, tests in every package)
- [x] Docs updated (API, security, architecture §5, ADR-0011, README) where behaviour changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens or personal data in code, tests or logs (the SeaweedFS key is local-only, like the Compose database password)

title: Phase 6a: issues, workflow, board, comments and history
body:
## What

Issue tracking (FR-4, first half): issues with a status workflow, a Kanban board, Markdown comments and a full change history, with the API and web pages for all of it. Attachments and notifications follow in Phase 6b.

## How

**Contracts (`@forge/types`)**
- The status workflow (`canTransition`), display labels, and issue-key parsing.
- Request and response schemas shared by the API and the web forms.

**API**
- Create, list, view (by id or by key, e.g. `PAY-14`), edit and soft-delete issues.
  - Numbers are allocated per project inside the transaction.
  - A new issue falls back to the project's default assignee.
- **Optimistic locking.** Each edit sends the `version` it last saw and is applied with a conditional update. A stale edit gets `409` instead of overwriting someone else's change. A no-op edit doesn't bump the version.
- **Workflow rules.** A disallowed move gets a `400` on `status`. `resolvedAt` is set when an issue enters Done or Cancelled and cleared when it leaves.
- **History.** Every field change, label, comment and lifecycle event is recorded, with the actor.
- **List.**
  - Filters: status, priority, type, assignee (`me`, `none` or an id) and label.
  - Full-text search with stemming, plus title substring matching, with wildcards escaped.
  - Sorted by updated, created or priority, with keyset pagination.
- **Comments.** Only the author, or a role with `comment:moderate`, can edit or delete. A deleted comment keeps its place in the thread but its text is no longer returned.
- New access-control scopes: `issueKey` and `comment`.

**Web**
- Issues and Board tabs on each project.
- **Issue list:** search, a status filter, sort, and "Assigned to me".
- **Create dialog.**
- **Board:** drag and drop, plus a "Move to…" menu so it works by keyboard. Only moves the workflow allows are offered.
- **Issue page:**
  - edit the title and Markdown description in place
  - a side panel that saves each change immediately, with a status list limited to allowed moves
  - comments and a history tab
  - a clear message when someone else changed the issue first
  - delete, for managers
- Markdown is rendered without raw HTML. Links open with `noopener noreferrer nofollow`.

## Testing

- A clean run of `pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test build --force` passed all 18 tasks:
  - Types: 117
  - API: 64 unit, 13 HTTP and 125 integration tests against real Postgres + Redis (18 new for issues)
  - Web: 53
  - AI service: 16
- The new integration tests cover numbering, the default assignee, field errors, role and outsider access, filters, search, pagination across all sorts, history events, stale `409`, the no-op case, the workflow and `resolvedAt`, soft delete, and comment permissions.
- **Concurrent-edit race:** exactly one of two simultaneous edits succeeds. Removing the version check makes this test fail 3/3.
- Web component tests cover:
  - board moves and rejected drops
  - allowed status options (these caught a duplicated option, now fixed)
  - sidebar saves, including the full label set and story-point validation
  - the create dialog
  - the history text
- Browser run against a fresh seeded stack, 14 steps, all passing:
  - list and search
  - creating an issue, with the description rendered as Markdown
  - editing each side-panel field and the title
  - comments: add, edit and delete
  - history
  - the conflict message across two sessions
  - a board move
  - a viewer sees everything read-only
  - an issue key under another project's URL shows "not found"
  - delete
  - no unexpected console errors

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes (lint, typecheck, tests in every package)
- [x] Docs updated (API, security, README) where behaviour changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens or personal data in code, tests or logs

title: Phase 5: project management (projects, members, labels, settings)
body:
## What

Project management (FR-3): create, list, view, update, archive and restore, and permanently delete projects; manage members and their roles; manage labels. It runs through the RBAC layer from Phase 4, with API endpoints and web pages for everything.

## How

**Projects**
- The creator becomes the first project manager, in the same transaction.
- The list shows your projects (admins see all), sorted by name with keyset pagination, search, and an active/archived filter.
- Projects are fetched by id or by key (the web app uses `/projects/PAY`).
- Keys are immutable once created.
- **Archived projects are read-only:** the guard answers `409` for every write except restoring, so no future feature can forget the check.
- **Permanent delete has three safety catches:** admins only, the project must be archived first, and the key must be repeated in `?confirm=`.

**Members**
- Add people by email with a role, change roles, remove members, or leave a project yourself.
- Role changes and removals take effect on the member's next request (the membership cache entry is invalidated).
- A project always keeps a manager. Demoting or removing the last one is refused, and the project row is locked so two managers demoting each other at the same moment can't both succeed. With the lock removed, the race test fails 3/3.

**Labels:** create, edit and delete; names are unique per project, ignoring case.

**Shared permission matrix:** it moved to `@forge/types`, so the web hides exactly the controls the API would reject. The API still enforces every request.

**Audit:** project lifecycle and membership events are recorded. `project.updated` records only the fields that actually changed; the browser run found that it had been listing every field the form sent.

**Web**
- Projects list, and a create form that suggests a key from the name.
- A project workspace with Overview, Members, Labels and Settings tabs, where Settings includes archive/restore and the admin-only delete.
- Controls are hidden when your role can't use them, and there are confirmation dialogs for irreversible actions.
- The home page lists your projects.

## Testing

- `pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test build --force` from a clean state: 18/18 tasks, **318 tests**.
  - Types: 90 (the full permission matrix now lives here).
  - API: 58 unit, 13 HTTP, 107 integration against real Postgres + Redis.
  - Web: 34.
  - AI service: 16.
- The 30 new integration tests cover:
  - every endpoint as manager, developer, viewer, outsider and admin
  - archived read-only behaviour
  - the last-manager rule, including the concurrent race
  - immediate access changes after role edits and removal
  - the delete safety catches
  - audit rows
- Browser run against a fresh seeded stack, 14 steps, including:
  - unknown-email and duplicate-label errors
  - role change, and a refused last-manager demotion (the select reverts and explains why)
  - rename, archive (banner shown, controls hidden) and restore
  - creating a project with the suggested key
  - a non-manager sees no management controls; a non-member sees "Project not found"

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes (lint, typecheck, tests in every package)
- [x] Docs updated (architecture, API, README) where behaviour changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens or personal data in code, tests or logs

title: Phase 4: authentication, sessions and role-based access control
body:
## What

Authentication and authorisation for the whole platform: FR-1 (register, login, refresh, logout, password reset, profile), FR-2.1 (admin user management) and the project RBAC layer from ADR-0002. There is an email worker for password resets and web pages for every flow.

## How

**Sessions** (ADR-0003, new ADR-0010)
- An ES256 access token (15 min) signed with `@nestjs/jwt`. The algorithm, issuer and audience are pinned; a forged `alg: none` token is rejected (tested). The web app keeps it in memory only.
- An opaque refresh token in an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie scoped to `/api/v1/auth`, stored hashed. It's rotated on every use. Replaying a used token revokes the whole session family; a replay within 10 s is treated as two tabs racing and gets `409`.
- A per-user revocation cutoff in Redis makes these take effect on the next request: deactivation, admin demotion, logout-everywhere, password change and password reset.

**Abuse resistance**
- Accounts lock after 5 failures and IPs after 20 (each per 15 min), with `Retry-After`.
- Redis rate limits send IETF `RateLimit-*` headers.
- Breached passwords are rejected via the HIBP k-anonymity API (fails open).
- No user enumeration: identical errors, equal timing via a dummy argon2 hash, lockout for unknown emails too, and reset requests always return `202`.
- CSRF: refresh and logout also check the `Origin` header.

**Authorisation**
- A global auth guard makes routes secure by default.
- `@RequireProjectPermission()` has a permission matrix defined in code and a 60 s Redis membership cache. Non-members get **404**, so project IDs can't be probed.
- Admin routes re-check the database rather than trusting the token claim.

**Email:** a BullMQ `email` queue and a separate `worker` process (`pnpm dev` starts both). Reset links are removed from Redis after delivery.

**Web:** login, register, forgot/reset password and the signed-in shell. React Hook Form uses the shared Zod schemas, with server field errors shown under their inputs. Refresh on 401 is single-flight. `proxy.ts` handles redirects.

**Found by testing and fixed:** the reset page's `Referer` header carried the reset token into the API's request logs. Request logs are now an allow-list, and the reset page sends `no-referrer` and removes the token from the URL.

## Testing

- `pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test build --force` from a clean state: 18/18 tasks, **267 tests**.
  - API: 114 unit (including the full permission matrix), 13 HTTP, and 88 integration against real Postgres and Redis (Testcontainers). Every auth flow and the RBAC matrix run over HTTP for PM, Developer, Viewer, outsider and admin.
  - Web: 20.
  - Shared types and AI service: 16 each.
- Mutation check: widening the reuse-grace window makes the theft-detection test fail.
- Browser run against a fresh stack, 11 steps:
  - validation, wrong password, sign-in
  - cookie flags, and no tokens in web storage
  - reload restores the session; sign-out ends it
  - the worker delivers the reset email to Mailpit; the reset through the emailed link works
  - the old password is rejected and the new one accepted; registration works
  - `token=` appears 0 times in the API, worker and web logs
- `pnpm dev` starts web, API, worker and AI service.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes (lint, typecheck, tests in every package)
- [x] Docs updated (architecture, API, README) where behaviour changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens or personal data in code, tests or logs

title: Phase 3: database schema, migrations and seed data
body:
## What

The PostgreSQL schema for the whole platform: 34 tables, one reviewed initial migration, a seed script with demo data, and integration tests against a real Postgres + pgvector. This implements architecture §8 and FR-4.1, FR-4.7, FR-5.1 and FR-13 at the database level. The design is explained in the new `docs/database.md`.

## How

- **Prisma 7.10** (stable; npm's `latest` tag currently points at an 8.0 RC) with the `pg` driver adapter and a CommonJS client generated into `src/generated` (gitignored; a Turbo `db:generate` task runs before every build).
- **Integrity enforced in the database, not only in code:**
  - Composite foreign keys make cross-project data impossible to create: a label from another project, an issue in another project's sprint, a vector chunk whose project differs from its document's.
  - Partial unique indexes allow one `ACTIVE` sprint per project (this holds under a concurrent race, which is tested) and one current sprint per issue, while keeping the full sprint history.
  - `CHECK`s keep status and timestamps consistent: `resolved_at` is set exactly when the issue is resolved, and sprint lifecycle timestamps match the sprint status. Others cover formats (project key, colours, SHAs, token hashes) and limits.
  - Triggers make `audit_logs` append-only; UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE are all rejected.
- **Gap-free issue numbers:** an allocator increments a per-project counter inside the insert transaction (`UPDATE … RETURNING`). Tested with 25 concurrent creates and with a rollback.
- **Search:** generated `tsvector` columns with GIN indexes, a trigram index on titles, and an HNSW cosine index on `vector(1536)`. The schema declares these, so `prisma migrate diff` reports **no drift**. A test and a CI step both check that.
- **Least privilege:** the `forge_ai` role can only reach the RAG tables. Compose creates its login from `.env`, so no password is in any migration.
- **Readiness fix (security):** `/health/ready` returned raw driver errors that named internal hosts and ports. It now returns `Unavailable` and logs the full error.
- **Seed data:** 6 users, 2 projects, 3 sprints (including one carried-over issue) and 17 realistic issues with comments and status history. It runs in a single transaction and refuses to run in production.
- **CI:** the compose job now applies migrations, checks drift, seeds twice (the second run must be a no-op) and verifies the AI role's permissions.

## Testing

- `pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test build --force` from a clean state: 18/18 tasks. API tests: 26 unit, 9 HTTP and 58 integration (Testcontainers, the same pgvector image as compose).
- I checked the drift test really catches drift: adding a column to the schema without a migration makes it fail.
- Fresh bootstrap in an isolated compose project (init scripts → migrate → seed → AI-role check), then torn down.
- Checked against seeded data:
  - velocity: Sprint 1 completed 16 points
  - burndown built from `issue_events`
  - full-text ranking
- The compiled `dist` API runs against Postgres. Readiness goes to 503 when Postgres is stopped and recovers when it restarts.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes (lint, typecheck, tests in every package)
- [x] Docs updated (architecture, API, README) where behaviour changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens or personal data in code, tests or logs

title: Phase 2: repository structure and configuration
body:
## What

Sets up the monorepo that every later phase builds on: three runnable services, shared packages, local infrastructure and CI. This implements the structure in `docs/architecture.md` §12. There are no domain features yet; those start in Phase 3.

## How

- **Monorepo:** pnpm workspaces + Turborepo. `pnpm lint | typecheck | test | build` runs across every package, including the Python service through a thin `package.json` wrapper.
- **`apps/api` (NestJS 11):**
  - environment variables validated with zod at startup
  - pino JSON logs that carry the request ID and redact credentials
  - RFC 9457 `problem+json` errors that don't leak internals on a 500
  - helmet, a CORS allow-list and Swagger
  - `/health/live` and `/health/ready`, where each dependency check has a timeout
- **`apps/web` (Next.js 16, Tailwind 4, TanStack Query):** the browser calls `/api` on the web origin and a rewrite forwards it to the API, as in architecture §3. A status card shows live API readiness.
- **`apps/ai-service` (FastAPI):**
  - app factory, so importing the module has no side effects
  - pydantic-settings, and structlog with the same request-ID rule as the API
  - service-token auth using a constant-time compare, and a minimum token length
  - tooling: uv, ruff, strict mypy, and pytest with warnings treated as errors
- **Shared packages:** `@forge/types` (zod schemas), `@forge/ui` (shadcn/ui) and `@forge/config` (tsconfig, ESLint flat config, Prettier).
- **Docker Compose:**
  - Postgres 16 with pgvector 0.8.6, Redis 7 with AOF persistence, and Mailpit
  - all ports bound to 127.0.0.1, all services with healthchecks
  - an init script installs the extensions and creates a separate test database
- **CI:** TypeScript, Python and Compose jobs. Also Dependabot with grouped updates, and this PR template.
- **New ADR-0009:** NestJS 11 / TypeScript 5.9 / ESLint 9. NestJS 12 is ESM-only, which conflicts with Jest. TypeScript 7 and ESLint 10 are outside the supported range of typescript-eslint, ts-jest and eslint-config-next.

## Testing

- `pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test build --force`: 17/17 tasks passed. `pnpm format:check` is clean and `uv sync --locked` succeeds.
- Tests: api 21 unit + 8 HTTP (Supertest), web 3 (Testing Library), types 7, ai-service 16.
- Manual end-to-end run against the real containers:
  - Readiness went through the web rewrite and returned 200.
  - Stopping Redis gave 503 with the reason while liveness stayed 200; restarting Redis brought readiness back to 200 on its own.
  - The AI service returned 401 without the token and 200 with it; the request ID was propagated.
  - `pnpm dev` hot reload works.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes (lint, typecheck, tests in every package)
- [x] Docs updated (architecture, API, README) where behaviour changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens or personal data in code, tests or logs
